title: Local Authoring Service And Publication Boundaries
summary: record why Studio and Docs Viewer remain separate local services, why their publication timing differs, the shared vocabulary, and evidence that would justify reconsideration
content_html:
Local Authoring Service And Publication Boundaries

Decision

Studio and Docs Viewer remain separate domain services composed by one local launcher and configuration environment. Their publication workflows retain different timing because they own different canonical units and public-consistency boundaries. They share explicit publication vocabulary and projection principles, not one server, one mutation authority, or one generic publication engine.

This is an accepted architecture reference. It records the current rationale and the evidence that would justify reassessment; it does not approve a server merge, launcher delivery, publication redesign, endpoint alias, or UI rename.

Context

The iPad local-authoring assessment made two existing differences more visible:

  • Studio and Docs Viewer require two loopback Python services even when they are used as one linked authoring environment; and
  • Studio has evolved towards refreshing public Catalogue products when an already-published record is saved, while Docs Viewer retains an explicit scope-wide Publish and a separate next-Publish inclusion filter.

Operational proximity does not itself imply shared authority. Server composition and publication semantics are separate architecture questions: the apps could share a process while retaining different publication models, or retain separate processes while using the same vocabulary.

iCloud Drive is synchronization transport for DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR, not a remote runtime dependency. When required content has downloaded and the configured folder is locally readable, the applications interact with ordinary local filesystem paths. Loss of network synchronization is therefore distinct from a missing configured base, an absent iSH Files-provider mount, or one unavailable external Docs Viewer scope.

Service Boundary

Current Ownership

service owns does not own
Local Studio /studio/ shell and routes, runtime config, Catalogue and Tag APIs, canonical Catalogue and Tag mutations, Studio lookups, scoped Catalogue builds, and confined project-media reads Docs Viewer source, document packages, Docs Review, public Docs projection, or the deployed public-site server
Docs Viewer /docs/, /docs-review/, document and package APIs, repository and external-local scope resolution, canonical document mutations, private document/search builds, and configured public Docs projection canonical Catalogue or Tag mutation, Studio route hosting, or the deployed public-site server
local launcher process composition, ports, environment, startup reporting, and coordinated shutdown domain validation, data mutation, projection planning, or recovery semantics

Local Studio App owns the Studio server boundary. Studio Runtime owns its browser composition. Source Organisation and the Docs Viewer service own the document-side topology and capabilities.

Why Separate Services Remain Justified

  • Docs Viewer supports repository and external-local scopes, package/review workflows, independently enabled capabilities, and a future independently composable boundary.
  • Each server owns distinct static-path containment, runtime configuration, API dispatch, startup checks, and failure reporting.
  • Studio and Docs Viewer retain different route, configuration, capability, mutation, and generated-product authorities even when used in one local session.
  • Cross-app links and focused observer integrations do not require a shared write authority or transaction.

The two ports are not treated as a strong security boundary. Both apps deliberately accept allowed loopback origins, so separation primarily provides ownership, capability, lifecycle, and independently composable operation. Per-scope availability is a Docs Viewer responsibility, not a reason to keep the servers separate.

External-Local Availability Contract

DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR is the configured local root shared by the integrated external workspaces. A missing, unmounted, unreadable, or invalid base is a whole-environment configuration condition. It is not equivalent to temporarily paused iCloud synchronization, and it is distinct from one configured external Docs Viewer scope root being absent or unreadable below an otherwise valid base and Docs workspace.

An unavailable exact external scope is a per-scope capability state. Docs Viewer must remain running, keep its shell and health route available, continue serving unrelated repository and available external scopes, retain the configured unavailable scope as an explicit unavailable record, and reject operations targeting only that scope with a clear browser-safe reason. Generated document and search availability remain separately observable; source unavailability must not be silently treated as an empty scope.

Service startup must not manufacture a partial external scope by creating media or published descendants below an absent scope root. Directory creation belongs to explicit scope lifecycle or an exact operation whose target has already passed its availability and ownership checks.

Selected external-scope operations continue to fail loudly when their required workspace is unavailable. Intentional all-scope builds and audits may also return non-success with exact incomplete coverage. Graceful interactive service availability does not mean swallowing a selected-scope failure, claiming a complete all-scope result, or falling back to another scope.

Composition Before Consolidation

The preferred operational model is one command that starts and stops the required sibling services while leaving their domain boundaries intact. bin/local-all is the current composition owner. A later environment-specific launcher such as bin/local-ipad may narrow enabled services and load a tested profile without moving routes or mutations between servers.

Shared low-level HTTP helpers may be extracted when repeated maintenance or inconsistent behavior proves a concrete need. That does not require one process. Do not create a generic local-app framework, route registry, proxy layer, compatibility alias, or merged service merely to remove visible duplication.

What A Merge Would Need To Resolve

A single host would need explicit decisions for:

  • the currently overlapping /health route and aggregate versus domain health;
  • overlapping static path families and exact serving ownership;
  • combined capability and configuration initialization;
  • independently enabled management, review, generated-read, Catalogue, and Tag capabilities;
  • process failure and shutdown behavior;
  • cross-domain runtime configuration and asset versioning;
  • preservation or retirement of independently composable Docs Viewer operation; and
  • continued separation of domain services even if HTTP dispatch shares a process.

Until evidence shows that these costs solve a real operational failure, one launcher with separate services is the smaller and safer architecture.

Shared Publication Vocabulary

Use these meanings across Studio and Docs Viewer:

term meaning
Canonical save Mutate the domain-owned editable source after validation.
Working projection refresh Rebuild local consumer products needed by the authoring application, such as Studio lookups or Docs Viewer private document/search payloads.
Eligibility State that determines whether canonical content participates in a later or current public projection; it is not proof of current public bytes.
Public projection refresh Materialize domain-owned consumer-ready public files from eligible canonical source at the domain's consistency unit.
Deployment Move or expose tracked public artifacts through the public hosting workflow; neither a local source save nor a local projection refresh is by itself internet deployment.

Remote media publication remains an additional provider-specific operation. A local public build and an R2 upload are separate failure and confirmation boundaries even when one UI action composes them.

The shared vocabulary does not require identical buttons, endpoints, metadata, or timing. Projection Contract remains the cross-system source/projection owner.

Current Publication Models

concern Studio Catalogue Docs Viewer public-capable collection
canonical editing unit one Work, Series, or Work-owned detail aggregate documents forming a parent scope or exact child collection
eligibility Work or Series status: published included by omission; explicit publishable: false excludes from the next Publish
draft or ordinary private save canonical source plus affected Studio lookup projections canonical Markdown plus private document/search projection
save when already public-eligible field-aware scoped public Catalogue refresh no public mutation; the prior public snapshot remains
positive promotion explicit Work or Series Publish changes canonical status and builds its affected public products explicit scope-wide Publish promotes the complete prepared eligible projection
negative removal Unpublish or Delete performs owned public cleanup canonical Delete immediately removes its exact public projection; publishable: false waits for the next scope Publish
deployment later tracked-site deployment; remote media has its own confirmed R2 path later tracked-site deployment

Catalogue Architecture owns Catalogue source and projection shape. Catalogue Work Editor and Catalogue Series Editor own current save and publication workflows. Publishable field owns the Docs Viewer eligibility contract.

Why The Timing Differs

Studio: Record-Level Continuous Refresh

A published Catalogue record expresses continuing public intent. Saving its canonical metadata therefore refreshes the affected public representation. The Catalogue field registry and build planner can select the exact Work, Series, index, search, page, and media artifact families affected by classified fields. A draft save remains source and lookup only.

This behavior is best described as continuous refresh of an already-published record, not as removal of the initial Publish decision. Explicit Publish still changes a draft into a published record; Unpublish reverses that state. Source save, public build, and remote media publication remain separately reportable and retryable even when Save composes them.

Docs Viewer: Explicit Scope Snapshot

A Docs Viewer public projection is a coordinated scope product rather than an isolated document payload. Parent hierarchy, descendants, sub-scope manifests, by-ID records, search, Recent, references, locations, public report hosts, and publication follow-through may need to agree. Working Markdown can continue to change while the previous public snapshot remains stable.

Scope-wide Publish is therefore the sole positive public mutation. It promotes the complete eligible scope snapshot deliberately. Per-save public mutation would change the editorial meaning of a Docs save and could expose incomplete document or collection work before the owning scope products are reconciled.

publishable Is Selection, Not Another Publish

Docs Viewer stores only the exception publishable: false; omission means included in the next scope-wide Publish. Set Publishable… changes that next-Publish selection and rebuilds the private working projection, but does not add, update, or remove a public file. The current public snapshot changes only through scope-wide Publish, apart from exact immediate cleanup after canonical Delete.

The contract therefore has one positive promotion action, not per-document and scope-level Publish actions. Nevertheless, Set Publishable… can sound like a publication-state transition. Its actual user meaning is Include in next Publish or Exclude from next Publish. Presentation may be reviewed if users mistake it for current-public evidence, review status, privacy, or a per-document Publish command. Such a review does not itself authorize a source-field rename or contract change.

Deliberate Non-Symmetry

Do not change either workflow merely to make the apps look alike.

  • Adding an explicit refresh gate to every Studio save would create a new stale-public state and editorial staging workflow. That requires a real need for review between canonical Catalogue save and public refresh.
  • Publishing a Docs document on every save would replace the established stable-snapshot editorial model and require proof that the complete scope consistency unit can be updated safely from an individual save.
  • Moving publishable into ordinary metadata or treating it as current publication state would conflate eligibility, source editing, and public evidence.
  • A shared generic publication engine would obscure the different transaction units, dependencies, cleanup rules, and failure boundaries.

Shared concepts should improve explanation, receipts, and cross-system reasoning while domain services retain their exact mutation planners.

Reconsideration Triggers

Service Composition

Revisit the separate-process decision only when evidence shows at least one of the following:

  • a supported environment cannot reliably keep the two child processes or loopback ports active;
  • cross-origin or multi-port behavior creates a persistent product failure that configuration and linking cannot solve;
  • a required operation needs a genuine atomic transaction across canonical Studio and Docs Viewer authorities rather than an existing post-commit observer or projection refresh;
  • duplicated HTTP infrastructure repeatedly causes inconsistent safety or runtime behavior; or
  • independently composable Docs Viewer operation is deliberately retired through its owning architecture decision.

Even then, assess a shared HTTP host with domain-separated adapters before merging services or data authority.

Publication Semantics

Revisit timing only when evidence shows at least one of the following:

  • Catalogue editors require a real review or staging interval between saving a published record and refreshing public output;
  • Docs Viewer requires and can safely support an independently consistent per-document public transaction;
  • scope-wide Docs Publish is operationally too expensive or prevents a required editorial workflow;
  • default-included Docs documents are repeatedly promoted unintentionally;
  • publishable is repeatedly used or understood as current-public evidence, editorial review state, privacy, or a second Publish action; or
  • current receipts cannot distinguish canonical save, working refresh, public projection refresh, remote media publication, and deployment clearly enough to diagnose failure.

These triggers authorize reassessment, not automatic convergence.

Current Consequences

  • Keep Studio and Docs Viewer route, API, configuration, and mutation ownership separate.
  • Use one launcher/profile for environments that need both apps.
  • Preserve exact cross-app links rather than proxying or importing sibling runtime modules.
  • Parse configured scope identity independently of exact provider availability, resolve only the scopes required by an operation, and report unavailable external scopes without terminating unrelated interactive service behavior.
  • Keep a missing configured projects base distinct from one unavailable external scope and from paused iCloud synchronization.
  • Describe Studio's published-record save as an automatic public projection refresh.
  • Describe Docs Viewer publishable as a false-only next-Publish exclusion and scope-wide Publish as the sole positive public mutation.
  • Keep deployment and remote media publication distinct from local public artifact generation.
  • Add implementation work only after one of the reconsideration triggers has concrete evidence and a bounded completion rule.
